metadata.title: SARVAX Enterprise AI Intelligence — Founder Validation Edition
metadata.decision: NO-GO for model procurement, pricing commitments, or production routing
metadata.scope: Entire canonical report, calculation layer, workflow data, QA pipeline, and inspected frontend contract
metadata.method: Claim-level classification with fail-closed evidence rules
metadata.external_research_status: Official-source retrieval blocked by execution permission during this run; no current external claim was promoted.
metadata.currency_status: LOCKED — no timestamped accepted USD/INR source
metadata.model_catalog_status: QUARANTINED — raw/secondary records are not deployment-approved

claims.claim: The report empirically evaluated 586 global models.
claims.reason: A raw third-party feed was ingested; ingestion is not an empirical evaluation and no per-model validation record exists.
claims.action: Removed from executive claims.

claims.claim: 37 models are verified frontier models.
claims.reason: The previous UI contained 35 models, the master file contained 37, and claim-specific vendor evidence was absent.
claims.action: Model ranking and pricing tables quarantined.

claims.claim: 1 USD = ₹96.61 is a live verified exchange rate.
claims.reason: The value was hardcoded; repository files also contain ₹83.50 and ₹83.05. No accepted timestamped FX evidence is stored.
claims.action: INR calculations locked until a timestamped source is ingested.

claims.claim: The prior report passed a 100% quality gate and was production-ready.
claims.reason: The previous validator checked string presence and file existence while browser interactions and evidence handlers were broken.
claims.action: Replaced with evidence-aware QA and a NO-GO decision.

claims.claim: Kimi K3 ranks first on TAU Banking with a 0.3340 score.
claims.reason: The claim is present in local data but lacks a preserved claim-specific benchmark payload and cross-source verification.
claims.action: Removed from routing decisions.

claims.claim: The proposed route saves ₹24.64 lakh annually per 100,000 reports.
claims.reason: The value depends on unverified model identities, prices, cache policy, token volumes, workload volume, and FX rate.
claims.action: Removed. Financial recommendations remain locked.

claims.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro has a strict 60 RPM limit that will trigger production HTTP 429 failures.
claims.reason: No official model/rate-limit evidence or measured load test is retained for this SKU.
claims.action: Converted to a generic capacity-test requirement.

claims.claim: Gemini 3.6 Flash has unlimited Vertex AI SLAs.
claims.reason: Unlimited service capacity is not a defensible cloud SLA statement; quota and provisioned-throughput terms are workload- and account-specific.
claims.action: Removed.

claims.claim: Six wealth workflows have exact token counts, costs, and 10,000-account monthly bills.
claims.reason: The values are scenario inputs, not measurements from representative production traces.
claims.action: Replaced by instrumentation requirements and explicit scenario labels.

claims.claim: A universal 80% cache-hit rate and 90% cache-read discount apply across selected models.
claims.reason: Cache eligibility, minimum prefix, TTL, write price, read price, and discount vary by provider and model.
claims.action: Simulator locked until model-specific cache evidence exists.

claims.claim: Displayed token, cost, latency, and cache savings are production telemetry.
claims.reason: Values were synthetic counters. Missing model IDs silently fell back to the first model, distorting cost.
claims.action: Simulator now demonstrates control flow only and labels all unmeasured telemetry as unavailable.

claims.claim: The prior five charts are empirical and suitable for model selection.
claims.reason: Chart values were embedded client-side without claim-level benchmark payloads, task definitions, dates, or confidence boundaries.
claims.action: Removed benchmark charts; added an audit-status visualization only.

claims.claim: EU AI Act Article 15 strictly prohibits INT4 for financial risk scoring.
claims.reason: Article 15 establishes accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity obligations; the report had no legal source establishing a blanket INT4 prohibition.
claims.action: Removed and replaced with outcome-based validation guidance.

claims.claim: Self-hosting in a private VPC guarantees 100% data sovereignty.
claims.reason: Sovereignty depends on identity, logging, backups, support access, keys, regions, subprocessors, and operating controls—not deployment location alone.
claims.action: Replaced with a control checklist.

claims.claim: Five virtual auditors unanimously approved the report with a 98.5/100 score.
claims.reason: No calibrated scoring rubric or independent human sign-off exists.
claims.action: Removed. Automated agents are listed as reviewers, not approvers.

claims.claim: The production product implements the report's 37-model central pricing and routing engine.
claims.reason: The inspected frontend exposes model selections and query allowances but does not prove the report's routing, pricing, or backend ledger logic.
claims.action: Separated current product evidence from target architecture.

claims.claim: One workflow run deducts one query or a known number of raw tokens from the user allowance.
claims.reason: The frontend exposes remaining/limit counters and can_make_query, but not the backend deduction algorithm.
claims.action: Marked backend accounting as an open evidence gap.

claims.claim: The UI contract exposes daily/monthly query limits, remaining balances, and can_make_query.
claims.reason: Directly observed in the inspected frontend API contract and usage UI.
claims.action: Retained with an internal-implementation evidence label.

claims.claim: Every metric exposes an eight-point evidence inspector.
claims.reason: Browser testing found openEvidenceModal and closeEvidenceModal undefined.
claims.action: Replaced with a working evidence drawer sourced from this claim register.

claims.claim: A versioned local source repository retains downloaded snapshots.
claims.reason: The registry references snapshot files that are absent; only source_registry.json is present.
claims.action: Knowledge-base status shown as incomplete.

claims.claim: The report is enterprise-accessible.
claims.reason: Previous modals lacked dialog semantics, chart alternatives, focus management, keyboard activation, and print styling.
claims.action: New report implements semantic controls, focus states, Escape handling, responsive tables, and print CSS.

claims.claim: String-presence checks prove links return HTTP 200 and JavaScript works.
claims.reason: The old QA suite did not perform network requests or execute interaction handlers.
claims.action: New pipeline distinguishes static integrity, browser behavior, and external evidence availability.

issues.title: No deployment-approved model or price corpus
issues.exit_criteria: Each deployed model has a current official model page, official rate card, content hash, retrieval timestamp, SKU match, and one independent benchmark record.

issues.title: Financial calculations depend on unverified FX, price, cache, token, and volume inputs
issues.exit_criteria: All inputs are source-backed; Python Decimal oracle and browser result reconcile exactly.

issues.title: Workflow telemetry was simulated and fallback routing corrupted costs
issues.exit_criteria: Unknown model IDs fail closed; traces provide measured token, latency, tool, retry, and route data.

issues.title: Backend credit deduction and reset policy are unknown
issues.exit_criteria: Trace ledger model, atomic deduction, failure/refund, reset timezone, organization pooling, and workflow charging.

issues.title: Local knowledge snapshots referenced by the registry are missing
issues.exit_criteria: Immutable snapshots exist, hashes match, diffs are reproducible, and unchanged content is not re-downloaded.

issues.title: Security and compliance assertions are not control-mapped
issues.exit_criteria: Vendor services and regions are mapped to official attestations, contract terms, data-flow diagrams, and customer control responsibilities.

workflows.name: Lab results inbox
workflows.purpose: Collect lab-result artifacts, extract fields, apply deterministic validations, update records, and prepare an approval-ready summary.
workflows.architecture: Deterministic orchestration with bounded model-assisted extraction

steps.name: Receive artifact
steps.control: Authenticate source and preserve original file hash.

steps.name: Extract document fields
steps.control: Use a verified multimodal/OCR service; retain page-level evidence.

steps.name: Validate schema and rules
steps.control: Reject missing, malformed, or out-of-range fields.

steps.name: Human approval
steps.control: Required before external writeback or communication.

steps.name: Write and audit
steps.control: Idempotent write, immutable event log, and rollback handle.

workflows.name: Daily operations summary
workflows.purpose: Aggregate verified events into a concise management view.

steps.name: Load verified events
steps.control: Use source timestamps and deduplicate event IDs.

steps.name: Compute KPIs
steps.control: All arithmetic runs outside the model.

steps.name: Draft narrative
steps.control: The model may explain calculated facts but cannot alter them.

steps.name: Publish internal view
steps.control: Show data freshness and missing-source warnings.

workflows.name: Repeat lot detection
workflows.purpose: Detect exact and near-duplicate lot identifiers across records.
workflows.architecture: Rules and database indexes first; model only for ambiguous text normalization

steps.name: Normalize identifiers
steps.control: Versioned normalization rules.

steps.name: Exact match
steps.control: Unique indexes and collision report.

steps.name: Ambiguity review
steps.control: No automatic rejection on fuzzy similarity alone.

workflows.name: Two-lab confirmation
workflows.purpose: Reconcile two independent lab results before a governed decision.
workflows.architecture: Evidence reconciliation with hard stop on conflict

steps.name: Ingest both reports
steps.control: Require independent source identity and complete artifacts.

steps.name: Extract comparable fields
steps.control: Attach bounding boxes or page references to each value.

steps.name: Reconcile
steps.control: Tolerance rules are explicit and versioned.

steps.name: Escalate conflict
steps.control: Conflicts never auto-resolve through model judgment.

workflows.name: Proactive lab communication
workflows.purpose: Draft a communication from verified lab status and approved policy.
workflows.architecture: Verified facts plus constrained drafting and mandatory approval

steps.name: Load approved facts
steps.control: No unsupported clinical or financial inference.

steps.name: Draft message
steps.control: Template and prohibited-claim checks.

steps.name: Approve
steps.control: Mandatory outbound approval.

steps.name: Send and log
steps.control: Only after explicit confirmation; store message ID and timestamp.

glossary.simple_definition: Units representing the prompt and supplied context.
glossary.technical_definition: Tokenizer-produced IDs processed during model prefill.
glossary.business_meaning: They drive context capacity, prefill latency, and usually input cost.
glossary.why_it_matters: They drive context capacity, prefill latency, and usually input cost.
glossary.analogy: Pages handed to an analyst before work begins.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, input tokens should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Measure actual provider usage; remove irrelevant context; never estimate billing from character count alone.

glossary.simple_definition: Units generated by the model.
glossary.technical_definition: Autoregressively decoded token IDs returned as visible or reasoning output according to provider accounting.
glossary.business_meaning: They drive response length, decode time, and usually higher unit cost.
glossary.why_it_matters: They drive response length, decode time, and usually higher unit cost.
glossary.analogy: Pages the analyst writes back.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, output tokens should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Set task-specific limits; require concise structured outputs; read provider reasoning-token rules.

glossary.simple_definition: Input plus provider-billed generated tokens for a defined request or workflow.
glossary.technical_definition: Usage metadata aggregated across model calls, retries, tool loops, and hidden reasoning where reported.
glossary.business_meaning: The variable meter behind model spend.
glossary.why_it_matters: The variable meter behind model spend.
glossary.analogy: Electricity consumed across every machine in a process.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, token consumption should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Meter per call and workflow; separate successful, failed, retried, and cached usage.

glossary.simple_definition: Provider reuse of a matching prompt prefix under provider-specific rules.
glossary.technical_definition: The service avoids some repeated prefill computation and bills cache writes/reads according to the SKU policy.
glossary.business_meaning: Can lower repeated-prefix cost and time, but only when requests are eligible and hits occur.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can lower repeated-prefix cost and time, but only when requests are eligible and hits occur.
glossary.analogy: A clerk reuses a verified standard binder instead of rereading it.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, prompt caching should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Model TTL, minimum length, write/read rates, and measured hit rate must be stored per SKU.

glossary.simple_definition: Maximum token sequence a model can process for a request under a specific API configuration.
glossary.technical_definition: The bounded attention and state budget shared by instructions, documents, tools, conversation, and generated tokens.
glossary.business_meaning: Determines whether data fits, not whether the model will use every part reliably.
glossary.why_it_matters: Determines whether data fits, not whether the model will use every part reliably.
glossary.analogy: Desk space, not memory quality.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, context window should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Reserve output headroom; test retrieval quality; prefer targeted context over indiscriminate dumps.

glossary.simple_definition: Vectors that encode semantic features of data.
glossary.technical_definition: Numeric representations compared with similarity metrics for retrieval, clustering, or classification.
glossary.business_meaning: Enable semantic search over internal content.
glossary.why_it_matters: Enable semantic search over internal content.
glossary.analogy: Map coordinates for meaning.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, embeddings should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Evaluate on domain queries; combine with keyword search for IDs, names, and exact values.

glossary.simple_definition: A store and index for vectors plus metadata.
glossary.technical_definition: A system that supports approximate or exact nearest-neighbor search with filters and lifecycle controls.
glossary.business_meaning: Retrieves candidate evidence quickly from large corpora.
glossary.why_it_matters: Retrieves candidate evidence quickly from large corpora.
glossary.analogy: A catalog that finds nearby meanings.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, vector database should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Enforce tenant isolation, source ACLs, deletion, versioning, and retrieval evaluation.

glossary.simple_definition: Retrieval-augmented generation.
glossary.technical_definition: An application retrieves evidence at request time and supplies it to a generator, usually with citations.
glossary.business_meaning: Updates knowledge without retraining and can improve grounding; it does not eliminate hallucination.
glossary.why_it_matters: Updates knowledge without retraining and can improve grounding; it does not eliminate hallucination.
glossary.analogy: An open-book answer with selected pages.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, rag should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Measure retrieval recall and answer faithfulness separately; expose source passages.

glossary.simple_definition: Retrieval using explicit entities, relationships, and graph-derived summaries.
glossary.technical_definition: A pipeline extracts a graph and uses neighborhood/community retrieval for multi-hop questions.
glossary.business_meaning: Useful when relationships matter more than isolated text similarity.
glossary.why_it_matters: Useful when relationships matter more than isolated text similarity.
glossary.analogy: A detective board connecting people, accounts, and events.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, graphrag should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Use only when graph construction quality and update cost are justified; preserve source links per edge.

glossary.simple_definition: Model Context Protocol.
glossary.technical_definition: A client-server protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to model applications.
glossary.business_meaning: Standardizes integration surfaces but does not replace authentication, authorization, or business logic.
glossary.why_it_matters: Standardizes integration surfaces but does not replace authentication, authorization, or business logic.
glossary.analogy: A common connector shape, not automatic permission.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, mcp should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Treat every server as a privileged integration; scope credentials, validate outputs, and log calls.

glossary.simple_definition: Model generation of arguments for an application-defined function schema.
glossary.technical_definition: The host provides schemas; the model proposes a function name and typed arguments; host code validates and executes.
glossary.business_meaning: Converts intent into controlled application actions.
glossary.why_it_matters: Converts intent into controlled application actions.
glossary.analogy: The model fills a form; software decides whether to submit it.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, function calling should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Validate authorization, ranges, identifiers, idempotency, and side effects outside the model.

glossary.simple_definition: A broader pattern in which a model requests external operations.
glossary.technical_definition: The runtime executes approved tools and returns observations for subsequent model turns.
glossary.business_meaning: Enables agents to act, while increasing security and reliability requirements.
glossary.why_it_matters: Enables agents to act, while increasing security and reliability requirements.
glossary.analogy: An analyst asks approved specialists for data.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, tool calling should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Allowlist tools, separate read/write permissions, require approval for irreversible actions, and cap loops.

glossary.simple_definition: Model outputs constrained to a declared schema.
glossary.technical_definition: Decoding or post-validation enforces a JSON-schema-like structure; semantic correctness remains separate.
glossary.business_meaning: Reduces parsing failures in integrations.
glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces parsing failures in integrations.
glossary.analogy: A completed form can still contain a wrong value.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, structured outputs should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Validate every field after generation; reject unknown enums, invalid dates, and unsupported claims.

glossary.simple_definition: Models optimized to spend more inference effort on multi-step problems.
glossary.technical_definition: They may use additional internal or exposed reasoning tokens and test-time compute.
glossary.business_meaning: Can improve hard problem performance at added cost and latency; benchmark fit is task-specific.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can improve hard problem performance at added cost and latency; benchmark fit is task-specific.
glossary.analogy: A specialist who takes more scratch-work time.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, reasoning models should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Route only evaluated tasks; keep deterministic math and policy checks outside the model.

glossary.simple_definition: A model architecture that activates a subset of expert blocks for each token.
glossary.technical_definition: A learned router selects sparse feed-forward experts while the full parameter set may still require storage.
glossary.business_meaning: Can improve capability per unit of active compute; deployment complexity remains.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can improve capability per unit of active compute; deployment complexity remains.
glossary.analogy: A dispatcher sends each case to selected specialists.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, mixture of experts (moe) should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Do not infer price, latency, or quality from MoE architecture alone.

glossary.simple_definition: Stored attention keys and values for previously processed tokens during inference.
glossary.technical_definition: It avoids recomputing prior sequence states during autoregressive generation; provider prompt caching is a separate commercial feature.
glossary.business_meaning: Improves decoding efficiency and shapes memory capacity.
glossary.why_it_matters: Improves decoding efficiency and shapes memory capacity.
glossary.analogy: Keeping working notes on the desk while writing.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, kv cache should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Separate runtime KV management from provider cache billing in documentation and telemetry.

glossary.simple_definition: Incremental delivery of generated events or tokens.
glossary.technical_definition: SSE, WebSocket, or chunked responses expose partial output before completion.
glossary.business_meaning: Improves perceived responsiveness but not necessarily total completion time.
glossary.why_it_matters: Improves perceived responsiveness but not necessarily total completion time.
glossary.analogy: Reading a document as pages arrive.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, streaming should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Handle cancellation, retries, partial JSON, moderation, and audit assembly.

glossary.simple_definition: A provider-specific asynchronous request facility.
glossary.technical_definition: Requests are submitted and retrieved later under SKU-specific pricing, eligibility, limits, and completion targets.
glossary.business_meaning: Useful for non-interactive workloads when delay is acceptable.
glossary.why_it_matters: Useful for non-interactive workloads when delay is acceptable.
glossary.analogy: Economy freight instead of same-day courier.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, batch api should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Verify the exact provider/model discount and SLA; never apply a universal discount.

glossary.simple_definition: Elapsed time for a defined operation.
glossary.technical_definition: Separate queue time, network time, time to first token, decode time, tools, retries, and orchestration critical path.
glossary.business_meaning: Determines user experience and SLA risk.
glossary.why_it_matters: Determines user experience and SLA risk.
glossary.analogy: Door-to-door travel time, not vehicle speed alone.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, latency should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Report percentile distributions from measured traces; simulations must remain labeled estimates.

glossary.simple_definition: Work completed per unit time under stated load.
glossary.technical_definition: Requests or tokens processed across concurrent workloads, constrained by quotas, batching, hardware, and latency targets.
glossary.business_meaning: Determines capacity and unit economics.
glossary.why_it_matters: Determines capacity and unit economics.
glossary.analogy: Customers served per hour.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, throughput should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Load-test with realistic concurrency; report both system throughput and per-user latency.

glossary.simple_definition: Additional training that changes model weights or adapters for a task or behavior.
glossary.technical_definition: SFT, preference optimization, or parameter-efficient methods train on curated examples.
glossary.business_meaning: Can improve consistency but adds dataset, evaluation, governance, and maintenance obligations.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can improve consistency but adds dataset, evaluation, governance, and maintenance obligations.
glossary.analogy: Training a general analyst on a house style.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, fine-tuning should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Use RAG for changing facts; tune only after prompts and retrieval are baselined; retain holdout evaluations.

glossary.simple_definition: A system that iterates across planning, tool use, observation, and control gates.
glossary.technical_definition: An orchestrator maintains state and invokes models/tools until completion, stop, or escalation.
glossary.business_meaning: Automates multi-step work but compounds errors and operational risk.
glossary.why_it_matters: Automates multi-step work but compounds errors and operational risk.
glossary.analogy: A supervised operator, not just a chatbot.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, agentic ai should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Bound scope, budget, steps, permissions, retries, and approvals; log every action.

glossary.simple_definition: Multiple specialized agents coordinated around a shared objective.
glossary.technical_definition: Agents exchange tasks or artifacts through an orchestrator, queue, or shared state with explicit conflict rules.
glossary.business_meaning: Can parallelize work, but coordination cost and correlated errors can erase gains.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can parallelize work, but coordination cost and correlated errors can erase gains.
glossary.analogy: A project team with defined roles and a manager.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, multi-agent systems should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Use only when decomposition is real; require independent evidence and deterministic merge rules.

glossary.simple_definition: Conversion of document images into machine-readable text and layout information.
glossary.technical_definition: OCR may combine image preprocessing, text detection, recognition, layout analysis, and confidence scores.
glossary.business_meaning: Required before text-only models can reason over scans.
glossary.why_it_matters: Required before text-only models can reason over scans.
glossary.analogy: A clerk transcribes a photographed form.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, ocr should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Benchmark on actual document types; retain page coordinates and confidence; route low-confidence fields to review.

glossary.simple_definition: Models that accept images or visual documents as input.
glossary.technical_definition: Multimodal encoders integrate pixel or patch representations with language generation.
glossary.business_meaning: Can interpret layout and images, but vision support does not prove OCR accuracy or compliance fitness.
glossary.why_it_matters: Can interpret layout and images, but vision support does not prove OCR accuracy or compliance fitness.
glossary.analogy: An analyst who can see the page, not necessarily read every character perfectly.
glossary.enterprise_example: In SARVAX, vision models should be used only inside a measured, governed workflow with source and audit records.
glossary.common_mistake: Treating the concept as a guarantee or applying provider-specific behavior universally.
glossary.best_practices: Evaluate extraction accuracy, layout, handwriting, small text, and adversarial content separately.

A can_make_query gate exists in the frontend contract.
The frontend contains model selection and workflow UI contracts.
The frontend alone does not prove backend routing, token metering, pricing, or deductions.

target.title: Recommended evidence-governed architecture
items: Deterministic orchestration owns state, policy, math, retries, and approvals.
Model gateway uses only verified SKUs and fails closed on unknown model IDs.
Tool gateway enforces identity, authorization, idempotency, and outbound approval.
Telemetry records provider usage, route, tools, retries, latency stages, cache events, and evidence IDs.
Finance engine reads versioned official rates and prices; HTML performs no business calculations.
Evidence registry stores immutable snapshots, hashes, claim links, retrieval dates, and supersession history.

financial_model.reason: No decision-useful INR value can be shown until model SKU, official input/output/cache rates, timestamped FX, measured token traces, and workload volume are all verified.
financial_model.formula: cost_inr = runs × Σsteps[((uncached_input_tokens × input_usd_per_million) + (cached_input_tokens × cached_read_usd_per_million) + (output_tokens × output_usd_per_million)) ÷ 1,000,000] × usd_inr
required_inputs: Input/output token usage from provider response
Cache-write/read eligibility and measured hit events
Scenario or measured monthly run volume

qa_expectation.acceptance_rule: The report can pass integrity QA while retaining a NO-GO executive decision. QA must never turn missing evidence into approval.
required_gates: No unsupported number presented as fact
No hardcoded business metric in HTML
Link and snapshot verification when network permission exists
